messages:
emma_support: Hey team — Nova Finance reported that after their BYOK key rotation yesterday we have gaps in audit logs: they see the rewrap API returning 200, but KeyVault/Azure Monitor shows no corresponding UnwrapKey events for a 30m window. Can someone triage?

raj_security: thanks @emma_support. do we have the exact timestamps + correlation id from their rewrap call? need CloudTrail/AzureDiagnostics time range. also wondering if this is an RBAC scope issue (service principal losing 'get' on key versions during rotation). :thinking_face:

emma_support: they pasted the root logs: 
```
{ "requestId": "f3a1-9b2d", "operation": "wrapKey", "status": 200, "timestamp": "2026-03-19T22:14:03Z" }
{ "requestId": "f3a1-9b2d", "operation": "rewrap", "status": 200, "timestamp": "2026-03-19T22:14:05Z" }
```
but AzureDiagnostics shows nothing for unwrapKey between 22:13-22:45.

mike_infra: can you confirm if they're using envelope rewrap (service does Encrypt locally then call KMS/KeyVault for wrap) or passing ciphertext to KV to rewrap? that changes audit surface.

emma_support: they say "server-side rewrap" — we call KeyVault: `POST /keys/{key-name}/{version}/unwrap` from our rewrap Lambda equivalent.

raj_security: ok. two quick checks: 1) service principal still has `keys/unwrap/action` permission on the NEW key version? 2) diagnostic settings on KeyVault might be scoped to a different retention/namespace — verify the diagnostic workspace + event categories include 'AuditEvent' and 'KeyVaultAudit'.

mike_infra: ran a quick check on their tenant with their consent. the service principal had correct role, but I noticed the diagnostics were piping to a Log Analytics workspace that had a retention-period policy with ingestion filter turned on. possible ingestion sampling dropped brief bursts.

emma_support: Nova pulled a clip from their app logs showing we did get `200` and returned wrapped blob to them, so the operation happened. they want a definitive tie between our rewrap call and KeyVault audit.

raj_security: also consider race where rotation created a new key version and our instance had an in-memory key-id cached; rewrap call may have gone to a different key resource (older version) which has diagnostic settings disabled. ask Nova to provide the exact `keyUri` (with version) from the request payload.

emma_support: asked them for keyUri + full request headers. they sent back: `https://nv-kv.vault.azure.net/keys/nova-byok/6f8a12b3c4` and headers include `x-ms-client-request-id: f3a1-9b2d`.

mike_infra: good. I checked that key version 6f8a12b3c4 has diagnostics turned on, but the subscription-level diagnostic sink had a transient throttling error at 22:14:04Z (Azure Monitor returned 429 for ingestion). that would explain missing entries in LA workspace.

deploy-bot: automated rewrap job (job-id: rw-20260319-004) triggered remediation: retried 3x, all returned 200, last retry 22:18:10Z.

raj_security: 429 ingestion plus retries explains why customer sees rewrap success but missing audit entries. impact: audit trail incomplete for that window — escalated to compliance for acceptance. action items: 1) notify customer that missing events due to ingestion throttling, 2) suggest enabling redundant diagnostic sink (Event Hub + LA) until retention/backfill confirmed, 3) add alert on Diagnostic Ingestion 429s.

olivia_docs: this is a docs gap — we should add an onboarding note about diagnostic sink configurations and ingestion throttling risks for BYOK rotations. tagging eng-infra for recommended alert defaults.

mike_infra: created an infra ticket: ENG-INFRA-4521 to add 429 detection and auto-replay of diagnostic fetch for 10m windows. I'll attach the snippet I used to check ingestion: 
```
az monitor diagnostic-settings show --resource-id /subscriptions/0000/resourceGroups/rg/providers/Microsoft.KeyVault/vaults/nv-kv --query "properties.eventHubAuthorizationRuleId"
# and check activity logs: az monitor activity-log list --start-time 2026-03-19T22:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-19T22:30:00Z --filters "status eq 429"
```

emma_support: customer asked if we can backfill the missing audit links on our side so they can satisfy their internal audit. is that feasible?

raj_security: short answer: we can surface our request traces (client-request-id, our outbound request logs) to correlate with KeyVault server responses. but we can't retroactively recover events that never ingested into their diagnostic sink. we can propose producing an exported correlation report listing our calls and responses for the timeframe.

emma_support: told them we'll provide correlation report + recommended mitigations. Nova asks for concrete checklist to prevent recurrence. can we draft one?

olivia_docs: drafting checklist now — will include: verify diagnostic settings, enable dual sinks (EventHub + LA), set retention and ingestion alerts, ensure service principal roles scoped to `keys/*` across versions during rotation, design rewrap retry/backoff, and run a post-rotation audit with sample rewraps.

mike_infra: I'll add an automated pre-rotation probe that runs a dummy unwrap against the new version and confirms LA entry before rotation completes.

raj_security: good. closing loop: compliance will need the correlation report and our remediation plan. @emma_support please attach logs + the job trace to the compliance ticket. :white_check_mark:

emma_support: will do. thanks everyone — following up with Nova about acceptance.
